rows: The stop check rightly objected that the `wf` suite passed only at a reduced worker count. Looping single files showed real races in the tests and mock helpers, several of them mine from the curl-to-server conversion: port files written in place and read while empty, one fixed port bound by two parallel files (and seeded as "nobody answers" in a third), a per-test server on a pid-derived port that the previous test's server could still hold, stub logs read before the stub wrote them, and a Chromium `beforeAll` that outlasted vitest's 10 s hook timeout under load. Each is fixed at its cause (atomic port files, unique ports or a free port chosen by the mock, `vi.waitFor` on the stub logs, `hookTimeout` 45 s, workers capped at cores minus one); the details are in `docs/audits/reports/tooling-wf-blackbox.md`. Tier: integration. The default `npx vitest run` passed 1153 of 1153 four times in a row (about 170 s each); before, most runs failed one to five tests, a different set each time. No behaviour of `wf` changed.
